questions.question: Which language should the Electron renderer use?

options.label: TypeScript
options.description: Typed application code for the React renderer and Electron integration.

questions.rationale: TypeScript is the practical default for a maintainable Electron POS app.

questions.question: Which frontend framework and desktop shell should the app use?

options.label: Vite + React + Electron
options.description: Fast local development with a familiar component model and desktop packaging path.

options.label: Plain Electron renderer
options.description: Minimal dependencies with manually managed DOM rendering.

questions.rationale: The requested screens and POS workflow benefit from React while Vite keeps setup simple.

questions.question: What first-version frontend features should be included?
questions.recommendedChoice: Login, dashboard, vehicle details, wash package selection, cart totals, payment completion state, and local session persistence.
questions.answer: Login, dashboard, vehicle details, wash package selection, cart totals, payment completion state, and local session persistence.
questions.rationale: These features cover the requested car-wash POS workflow without adding backend or cloud dependencies.

sharedQuestions.question: Which data stores does the first version require?

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use in-memory state and lightweight local storage only; no database service.

options.label: SQLite
options.description: Add a local embedded database for durable operational records.

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Store files or media outside the application.

sharedQuestions.rationale: The first version is local-first and only needs transient workflow state plus optional local session persistence.

sharedQuestions.question: Should users sign in before accessing the application?

options.label: Yes
options.description: Show a local login screen before the dashboard.

sharedQuestions.rationale: A login screen is explicitly part of the requested first-version scope; credentials remain local and demonstrative.
